Open the courtyard toward the verified access side to produce an entry-facing threshold.
Increase the void size so it functions as usable public space rather than a minor cut.
Reduce the sealed overhang condition at the base to strengthen the active ground relationship.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant subtraction into a real public void/court to establish the active ground threshold required by the neighborhood program.
Align the court opening to the verified access side in the program frame so the frontage becomes legible.
Widen the court enough to read as usable public space rather than a decorative chip.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact, coherent mass in individual views, but the four-view set does not convincingly reconcile into a strong neighborhood-living massing. The form is dominated by a steep, somewhat arbitrary stepped/twisted block that feels closer to a sculpted object than a building organized around an active public ground edge and usable void. The blue frontage edge is not answered by a legible entry seam, court, or undercut; instead the ground condition appears mostly sealed. The green parcel is respected, but the mass seems to fill it as a generic object rather than deriving a clearer site-responsive gesture. There is some hierarchy and a hint of top-setback continuity, but the open-space figure is weak and the section does not communicate the required neighborhood/public threshold logic. Reference resonance is moderate in the terraced/courtyard family, but the candidate remains too box-like and too internally arbitrary to pass program fit.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a more coherent pavilion-like cultural building; candidate is far more compact and boxy.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Carved central void with bridge-like upper connection and softened parapet profile can support neighborhood/public program.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a usable courtyard suggests a public ground sequence and hierarchy.

warnings: Form coherence is acceptable in isolation but weak across views; the object reads more as a clipped mass than a resolved site-building.
Road frontage response is semantically opposite to the brief: no clear public void or entry threshold at the verified access edge.
The visible section does not yet support the neighborhood-living contract of active ground, one clear public void/terrace, and calm upper massing.
